* If the main controller crashes, the backup servers vote on a new leader. Even after this election finishes, reading data might still show outdated information.
* The payment system prevents duplicate charges (it is idempotent) only if a retry uses the exact original tracking ID (the idempotency key).
* If your request times out, it is unknown whether the first payment went through. 
* Retrying with a new key is not protected by this guarantee and can charge the customer twice.
* When the system slows down incoming traffic (backpressure) to let waiting tasks clear, it only limits new requests; it does not cancel tasks it already accepted.
